candidates.name: Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma
support_spans: multiple pleural thickenings and marked effusion on the left side
Epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures
Immunoreactive for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, Wilms tumor protein 1
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with pleural thickenings and effusion, along with the pathological findings of epithelioid solid formations and immunoreactivity for mesothelial markers, supports this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Metastatic Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma
support_spans: Nodular growth observed on the mid third of the tongue
Neoplastic subepithelial proliferation, consisting of epithelioid cells in the tongue
Neoplastic cells immunoreactive for calretinin, confirming mesothelial origin
candidates.why: The appearance of a nodular growth on the tongue with pathological findings consistent with mesothelioma suggests metastatic disease.

candidates.name: Sarcomatoid Mesothelioma
support_spans: Absence of nuclear staining for BRCA1-associated protein 1
Homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene by fluorescent in-situ hybridization
candidates.why: The absence of nuclear staining for BRCA1-associated protein 1 and the homozygous deletion of the CDKN2A gene may suggest a sarcomatoid subtype of malignant mesothelioma, which can have a more aggressive clinical course.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because sarcomatoid mesothelioma is a rare and aggressive subtype of malignant mesothelioma, and the patient's clinical presentation and pathological findings may not be typical of this subtype.
